supporting_observations.claim: At 14:18:47 UTC, a Windows 4648 event on WS-GLUND-01 records SYSTEM running PowerShell with svc-docsync as the target account and DC-MAP-01 as the target server.

The event is consistent with an explicit-credential use from a help-desk workstation, whereas the provided inventory identifies svc-docsync as a DocSync job account on FILE-MAP-01. This warrants investigation but does not by itself establish malicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection were unavailable on DC-MAP-01 and FILE-MAP-01 from 13:25 to 14:20 UTC, overlapping most of the review window and the reported alert time.
The available evidence contains only one relevant event; it does not provide the domain-controller authentication results needed to verify repeated failures.
The available record does not show the PowerShell command line, the source of the credentials, or whether authentication succeeded.
claims_not_established: That repeated failed domain logons occurred; the available event does not record a failure result.
That the 4648 event was malicious or unauthorized.
That svc-docsync authentication succeeded, or that the password rotation and DocSync job update caused the event.
Who initiated or configured the PowerShell process running as SYSTEM.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain DC-MAP-01 authentication events for 13:20–14:20 UTC, including failed and successful logons for svc-docsync.
Obtain FILE-MAP-01 logs and DocSync job history for the same period, including evidence of the scheduled password rotation and manual job update.
Collect WS-GLUND-01 process-creation and PowerShell logs around 14:18 UTC, including command line, parent process, and task or service context.
Confirm whether the credential use from WS-GLUND-01 was an authorized troubleshooting or update action.
